summary: Split-horizon DNS returning CNAME loop causing control-plane service-discovery fallback and model-pull delays
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent platform slowdowns and model-pull delays on their Private deployment. Symptoms are control-plane service-discovery fallbacks, long model shard fetch latency (20–90s), and elevated retry counts which surface as downstream 429s from the hosted API layer. Issue appears restricted to a subset of nodes behind a corporate DNS forwarder.

Impact:
- FinTrust customer VPC procs experience degraded inference latency and periodic timeouts for long-lived streaming requests.
- Affecting production workloads in us-east-1; roughly 12% of serving nodes observed with repeated retries in the last 3 hours.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering to Redwood control plane).
- Customer-managed split-horizon DNS; forwarding to corporate resolvers for internal hostnames.
- Firewall/NAT egress appliance in front of resolver path.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Deploy a short burst of streaming requests that open long-lived gRPC sessions (alpha test harness attached).
2) Observe initial control-plane discovery requests for control.redwood.ai resolvable via customer's resolver.
3) On ~1 out of 8 nodes, resolver path returns a CNAME chain that eventually references the same control-plane name (CNAME -> CNAME -> control.redwood.ai). Client enters repeated name-resolution retry loop and falls back to alternate routable IPs; once fallback triggers, model-pull latency jumps and retries increase.

Observed behaviour:
- Repeated dig lookups via the customer's forwarder show an infinite/looping CNAME chain only when the query is forwarded to their on-prem resolver.
- The loop occurs only when EDNS client subnet is set (corporate resolver behavior). When queries are stubbed to cloud resolver, lookups resolve normally.

Expected behaviour:
- Control-plane service discovery should receive an A/AAAA record or a finite CNAME chain resolving to an A/AAAA record; no loops. Client should not be placed into a name-lookup retry fallback loop.

Attachments / logs (abridged):
- Sample dig output captured from affected node (dig +trace +edns @corp-resolver control.redwood.ai):
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
; control.redwood.ai. IN CNAME
control.redwood.ai. 60 IN CNAME ctl.internal.cust.local.
ctl.internal.cust.local. 60 IN CNAME control.redwood.ai.
;; loop detected: CNAME chain cycles back to control.redwood.ai

- tcpdump for DNS over UDP shows truncated responses (TC set) on some paths and the corporate resolver substituting alternative CNAMEs when EDNS client-subnet present.

Why this is unique / likely root cause hypothesis:
- Split-horizon zone misconfiguration on customer's corporate DNS: an internal CNAME points back to the external hostname instead of an internal A record. The forwarded EDNS-based path causes different resolver behavior (observed only when ECS/EDNS is set), producing a cyclical CNAME that our client doesn't detect as a permanent failure and instead retries name resolution frequently, triggering fallback to alternate endpoints and increasing model-pull latency.

Customer note:
- They recently introduced an internal migration that consolidated several hostnames and relied on CNAMEs to avoid changing external certificates; this change aligns with when the problem started.

Runbook references:
- See related confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dns-troubleshooting
comments: 2026-03-12 15:22 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage. Customer reports latency spikes; collected dig and tcpdump samples. Noted CNAME loop in dig output. Escalating to SRE for control-plane retry logic review.

2026-03-12 16:05 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed CNAME cycle in provided dig. Confirmed affected nodes are all using customer resolver path. Added packet captures and requested corp DNS zone files from customer for validation. Asked customer to temporarily stub resolver to 1.1.1.1 to confirm behavior — customer agreed to test.

2026-03-12 17:10 - FinTrust NetOps (Customer): Performed test: when nodes use 1.1.1.1, no loop observed and model-pull latency returns to baseline. When using corporate forwarder, loop reproduces. Provided split-horizon zone snippet and described recent consolidation change.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Implemented temporary mitigation in runtime: if a CNAME chain cycles more than 2 hops, abort lookup and fail fast with a distinct error for visibility (will be rolled back after customer fix). Observed immediate reduction in retry storm and normalized downstream 429s. Planning follow-up change to add client-side loop-detection metric.

2026-03-13 12:00 - Maya Chen (Support): Coordinating with CS to monitor customer after fix. Customer to update DNS zone to replace the internal CNAME with an internal A record for ctl.internal.cust.local.
investigation_notes: Checked control-plane resolver logs: spikes in NAMEERROR and repeated NXDOMAIN are not present; instead we see elevated retry attempts from certain node IPs in the customer's VPC.
Verified the problem is resolver-path dependent: public recursive resolvers do not reproduce the CNAME cycle.
Packet captures show TC (truncated) flags in responses from the corporate forwarder in 2/5 reproductions — suggests path MTU or response truncation influencing resolver rewrite behavior.

Applied temporary client-side defensive change to detect CNAME cycles > 2 hops and return actionable error to caller. Observed immediate reduction in repeated name resolution attempts and downstream retries.

Customer-supplied zone file excerpt shows: ctl.internal.cust.local. IN CNAME control.redwood.ai. — which creates the cycle when control.redwood.ai maps to ctl.internal.cust.local in their split-horizon view.

Recommended customer fix: replace CNAME with internal A/AAAA pointing to internal IP(s) or add explicit A/AAAA records in split-horizon zone for control.redwood.ai that don't reference an external CNAME.
resolution: Mitigation applied: runtime was updated to detect and abort cyclical CNAME chains (temporary defensive guard). Customer confirmed they will update split-horizon zone to remove the circular CNAME and replace with internal A records. Follow-ups: (1) monitor for recurrence for 72 hours, (2) revert defensive guard after customer fix and add a metric to detect cyclic CNAMEs in our telemetry. Postmortem to be created if issue reoccurs.
final_notes: Customer accepted workaround and scheduled DNS zone change for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Assigned follow-up action to Product to add a telemetry metric for CNAME loop detections and to Support runbook to include EDNS-based resolver checks.
priority_reason: P1 assigned due to production inference latency impact and increased downstream retries returning 429s for customer traffic.
